Treasury secretary compares upgrades to a vaccine

As the Americans can preparing to travel for Thanksgiving, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that the disruptions in technology may continue as companies and government agencies are modernising their systems for the age of artificial intelligence. Appearing on CNN’s “State of the Union,” Clayton said outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI era. He said the public should expect heavy investment in upgrading systems and in cybersecurity, and that any major leap in technology, in computing power or applications, brings disruption. People should understand that systems will be upgraded and may be interrupted for a time, he said, and that companies and the government are dealing with the problem proactively.Speaking on CNN's State of the Union, Clayton said the public should expect temporary interruptions as organisations invest heavily in new technologies and cybersecurity measures. "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said, according to a CNBC report.He added that people should understand that system upgrades may occasionally result in service interruptions while both government agencies and private companies work to strengthen infrastructure and security. "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he said.Government officials have largely dismissed the idea that the outages are linked to a coordinated cyberattack or one driven by artificial intelligence. The disruptions also slowed some bank transactions.A technology failure triggered a nationwide ground stop for flights just over a week ago that lasted for hours. The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades produced a flood of data that caused the stoppage, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack. Microsoft separately said its Outlook outage resulted from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message during an appearance on CBS' Face the Nation, urging Americans not to worry about the security of their financial institutions. Asked whether consumers should be concerned about banks, Bessent replied, "No, they shouldn't."Referring to software updates and security improvements designed to protect systems against emerging AI-related threats, he acknowledged that occasional glitches may occur."The patches may cause a glitch," Bessent said. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."
Article Summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says companies and government are upgrading systems for the age of artificial intelligence. Clayton said the public should expect temporary interruptions as organisations invest heavily in new technologies and cybersecurity measures. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Americans not to worry about their financial institutions.

Article Title: LinkedIn jobs, secret targets: How Trump's mass layoffs may have opened doors for Chinese spies
Article Text:
Trump administration's mass layoffs may have widened the pool of former US officials targeted by suspected Chinese spies through fake companies and LinkedIn job offers

How Trump 's mass layoffs created larger pool of potential targets

How suspected Chinese spy network operates

Former Pentagon official approached with paid assignment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Suspected Chinese intelligence operatives are using fake companies and job offers on platforms such as LinkedIn to target current and former US government officials, seeking access to sensitive information. Hundreds of suspicious websites identified, according to a report published in the CNN.The network has expanded as thousands of federal employees left government jobs during President Donald Trump 's first year back in office, leaving many without adequate guidance on how to identify and avoid such approaches.The suspected operation relies on fake consultancy firms that advertise lucrative research and consulting assignments. Former government officials and private consultants are approached through professional networking platforms and asked to prepare reports on issues related to China and other areas of interest. In some cases, those taking up the assignments do not know who the actual client is.Hundreds of thousands of workers left the federal government through firings, resignations and other means during Trump's first year back in the White House.The departures created a larger pool of unemployed people in the Washington, DC, area, including former officials who held security clearances and had access to sensitive government information.Foreign powers, including China and Russia, responded by stepping up efforts to recruit Americans working in national security, particularly those who had been fired or feared losing their jobs, CNN reported.“We created a vulnerability that was not necessary,” a former senior US intelligence official said, as quoted by CNN, referring to the mass layoffs. “We created access and opportunity to tens of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands, of people without the tools needed to deal with the Communist Party of China.”The fake companies typically use artificial intelligence and stolen identities to create professional-looking corporate websites, according to court documents. They then post vague but well-paying consulting jobs on platforms such as LinkedIn, often seeking people with expertise in China-related issues.Applicants may be asked to prepare research reports for the companies without knowing who is commissioning the work. While an individual report based on publicly available information may reveal little, intelligence officials say a large collection of such reports could help build a detailed picture of US national security policy and its vulnerabilities.The FBI seized 13 websites in June that officials said were linked to fake consulting firms. However, an analysis by CNN and Max Lesser, a senior analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, found several more suspicious websites with links to the seized domains.Lesser has identified more than 100 other web domains that share characteristics with the websites taken down by the FBI. Many remained online months after he publicly revealed them in November 2025, although several have since gone offline.“Those 13 domains are just the tip of the iceberg,” Lesser told CNN. Seizing them is “necessary but not sufficient,” he added, calling for faster action when suspicious domains are reported.The FBI said it was continuing to investigate the activity and take authorised steps to address the threat. China has denied the allegations. A spokesperson for its embassy in Washington said: “I am not familiar with what you mentioned. China opposes vilifying China by peddling the so-called ‘Chinese spy’ narrative.”One of the people approached was Wes Bryant, a former Air Force master sergeant who worked in a Pentagon office focused on reducing civilian harm during military operations. He said he was forced to resign in spring 2025 after criticising cuts to his office.In January 2025, Bryant received an email from someone claiming to represent a Malaysian think tank called MRDA. The sender expressed interest in his military experience and proposed collaboration on regional security issues.After leaving the Pentagon, Bryant decided to test the offer while checking the organisation with former colleagues. He prepared a report on how the Trump administration might approach a security pact with Australia and the UK, using only publicly available information.The purported representative, identified as Lily, paid him $1,200. She later said the unnamed client believed there was “room for improvement” in the report. Bryant suspected this was an attempt to draw out more sensitive information. Former colleagues subsequently told him that MRDA did not exist and that Lily had contacted other Pentagon employees.The Foundation for Defense of Democracies found that MRDA's website used a Chinese-language font and that images posted by one of its representatives carried watermarks from the Chinese social media platform RedNote. Researchers at the University of Toronto's Citizen Lab described the organisation as “likely China-related”, but said they had not found conclusive digital evidence linking it to the Chinese government.Another target, global affairs consultant Andres Loretdemola, said he was contacted on LinkedIn in 2025 by a woman offering up to $1,000 for reports on Russian affairs and geopolitics. He became suspicious after she appeared more interested in his connections with Washington think tanks.Loretdemola shared a recording of their conversation with the FBI. The bureau said the messages he provided were consistent with the pattern of activity described in the warrant used to seize the websites.The use of fake consultancies to approach US officials is not new. In 2018, Singaporean Dickson Yeo set up a fake company and advertised jobs, according to the US Justice Department. Ninety per cent of the resumes he received were from US military and government personnel with security clearances. Yeo was later sentenced to 14 months in prison after pleading guilty to acting as an agent of Chinese intelligence.US officials said the growth of artificial intelligence and the popularity of professional networking platforms have made such operations more effective.A LinkedIn spokesperson said creating fake accounts or misrepresenting one's identity violates the platform's terms of service. “We remain focused on detecting state-sponsored abuse and will continue to enforce our policies against fake accounts,” the spokesperson said as quoted by CNN.The US and its Five Eyes intelligence partners, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the UK, warned in June that information acquired through such schemes could put frontline military personnel at risk, weaken economic prosperity and enable interference in democratic processes.
Article Summary: Hundreds of suspicious websites identified, according to a report published in the CNN. The network has expanded as thousands of federal employees left government jobs during President Donald Trump's first year back in office. The departures created a larger pool of unemployed people in the Washington, DC, area.

Article Title: No fitness certificates for commercial vehicles without reflective tapes in Bihar
Article Text:
State transport commissioner Arif Ahsan at a Bihar Road Safety Council meeting on Monday

Patna

:





Commercial vehicles in Bihar will not be issued fitness certificates unless they have reflective and rear marking tapes meeting prescribed standards, as the transport department has tightened road safety measures ahead of winter fog. The move aims to improve visibility at night and during fog, when the risk of accidents rises.The directive was issued at a Bihar Road Safety Council meeting chaired by state transport commissioner Arif Ahsan on Monday. Officials from the transport, home, road construction, rural works and education departments, along with NHAI representatives, reviewed ongoing safety initiatives and compliance with earlier directives.Ahsan said poor visibility during winter made vehicles more vulnerable to collisions, particularly at night and on highways. He asked districts to strictly enforce the reflective tape requirement on commercial vehicles. Awareness campaigns will also encourage private vehicle owners to install reflective tapes, he said.Motorists have also been urged to drive cautiously in fog, maintain controlled speeds and safe distances, use fog lights appropriately and avoid unnecessary overtaking.Bihar recorded 12,615 road accidents in 2025, resulting in 10,349 deaths. Of these, 3,438 fatalities occurred between Nov and Feb, highlighting the heightened risks during winter.Officials also reviewed road safety engineering measures at accident-prone locations, including zebra crossings, road markings, rumble strips and speed breakers. Departments were asked to expedite pending work and ensure regular monitoring.The progress of foot overbridges, vehicle underpasses and pedestrian underpasses being built or improved under the road construction department and NHAI was also reviewed. Officials were directed to speed up these projects and strengthen safety infrastructure at vulnerable stretches.The transport commissioner stressed that road safety rules should be followed not merely to avoid penalties but to protect lives.
Article Summary: Commercial vehicles will not be issued fitness certificates unless they have reflective and rear marking tapes meeting prescribed standards. The move aims to improve visibility at night and during fog, when the risk of accidents rises. The directive was issued at a Bihar Road Safety Council meeting chaired by state transport commissioner Arif Ahsan on Monday.

Article Title: Stray dogs maul 8-year-old to death in Amritsar village
Article Text:

AMRITSAR: An eight-year-old boy was mauled to death by stray dogs in Jallal village in Baba Bakala tehsil of Amritsar district on Monday while he was on his way to the playground from his school.The incident has triggered an outrage among villagers who demanded immediate compensation for his impoverished family and a check on the population of the stray dogs.According to reports, the victim, Ranjit Singh, was reportedly chased by a pack of stray dogs on his way to the playground from school at around 11am on Monday."He ran towards the village playground in an attempt to escape, but the dogs caught hold of him and mauled him severely. His body was later found lying in the ground by children who had gone there to play. They alerted villagers, who rushed to the spot," said village resident Rachpal Singh.The attack left the child with severe injuries to his head and legs. According to villagers and police, the dogs had also eaten away his right ear. The family said Ranjit died on the spot.Calling it an extremely unfortunate incident, Rachpal said Ranjit was the youngest of four siblings."Last year, during heavy rains, the roof of their house collapsed. The family had applied for compensation, but due to an error in the name, they did not receive the assistance they were entitled to. The government should provide compensation for the loss of the child without further delay," he said.Police said the body was taken to hospital and required proceedings were initiated.The police said they would write to the concerned department to take steps to check the stray dog menace and also apprise the Deputy Commissioner of the incident.

Article Title: Golan Heights 2.0? Why Israel's grip on southern Lebanon is raising fears
Article Text:
Israeli soldiers walk through a village in southern Lebanon (David Cohen/Flash 90)

Fears of another Golan Heights

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Israel moved into southern Lebanon to create a security buffer between its northern border and Hezbollah . It aims to keep the militant group and its weapons away from Israeli communities.But what was projected as a military measure to prevent cross-border attacks is increasingly raising fears of a prolonged occupation.With Israeli forces establishing fortified positions and preparing for an extended presence, questions are mounting over whether the security zone could become permanent, much like the Golan Heights, which Israel captured from Syria in 1967 and has controlled for nearly six decades.The concerns have gained fresh momentum after an Israeli military spokesperson visited a school in Debl, a Christian-majority village inside the Israeli-controlled zone in southern Lebanon.Lt Col Ella Waweya, also known as Captain Ella, shared footage of the visit on social media. The video showed her interacting with students inside the school, which lies within the Israeli-controlled security zone.Waweya reportedly praised the beauty of southern Lebanon's villages while blaming Hezbollah for the destruction and suffering in the region.Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam strongly condemned the visit, accusing the Israeli military of exploiting schoolchildren for propaganda and attempting to legitimise its presence in southern Lebanon."The use of students in a military and propaganda display constitutes a violation of the sanctity of schools and children's rights," Salam said in a statement carried by Lebanon's National News Agency."An occupying power has no right to exploit our children to embellish the image of its occupation or impose its dominance over our people in the south," he added.The Debl municipality clarified that Waweya's visit had taken place around a month earlier, without prior coordination with the school's administration.Israeli forces currently occupy approximately 600 square kilometres of Lebanese territory, accounting for nearly 6 per cent of the country, according to a November 18 report by Defense News citing the UN peacekeeping force UNIFIL.The Israeli-controlled zone extends up to around 10 km inside Lebanon in some areas and includes military positions and fortified bases. UNIFIL has also reported continued Israeli construction of military positions and roads, demolitions and military operations inside Lebanese territory.The Golan Heights offers a telling precedent for what could lie ahead for southern Lebanon.What began as an Israeli military capture of Syrian territory during the 1967 Six-Day War gradually turned into a decades-long occupation, with Israel extending its laws and administration to the territory in 1981.Nearly six decades later, Israel continues to control the strategic plateau despite international opposition. Now, as Israeli forces establish fortified positions and prepare for an extended presence in southern Lebanon, fears are growing that the declared security zone could follow a similar trajectory.Experts have warned that the distinction between a temporary security buffer and a prolonged occupation could become increasingly blurred.Gustav Meibauer, an assistant professor of international relations at Radboud University, told DW that the name given to such a zone matters less than what is happening on the ground."What matters is not what something is called, but what is being done", he said.Meibauer warned that if the Israeli military presence becomes a de facto permanent arrangement, with territory rendered uninhabitable and remaining under Israeli control, it could amount to an occupation under international law.HA Hellyer, a senior fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), also raised concerns that Israel could be using the current situation to establish new territorial realities in southern Lebanon."They're using this particular period to draw some new lines in the sand, to create these sort of security zones," Hellyer told DW.He pointed to the Golan Heights as an example of how Israeli security zones and territorial control could develop into long-term arrangements.The question of how long Israel intends to remain is also becoming a diplomatic flashpoint.Israeli Defence minister Israel Katz has said that Israeli forces will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed and has ordered preparations for an extended military presence.Washington has pushed back, with a US state department official saying that a permanent Israeli military presence in southern Lebanon would not be consistent with the commitments made under the agreement between the two countries.For now, Israel has not announced any plan to annex southern Lebanon, and its stated objective remains the removal of Hezbollah's threat along its northern border.However, its expanding military footprint, preparations for a prolonged presence and the destruction of border villages have raised questions about whether the security zone could outlast the current conflict.With the Golan Heights serving as a historical precedent, the central concern for Lebanon is whether a buffer zone created in the name of security could eventually become a decades-long Israeli occupation.
Article Summary: Israel moved into southern Lebanon to create a security buffer between its northern border and Hezbollah. Fears are mounting over whether the security zone could become permanent, much like the Golan Heights, which Israel captured from Syria in 1967 and has controlled for nearly six decades. Israeli forces currently occupy approximately 600 square kilometres of Lebanese territory.

Article Title: Karnataka Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submits resignation over elephant relocation to her constituency
Article Text:
Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation letter due to the elephant relocation issue in her constituency

56 elephants move through Hassan, Chikkamagaluru

Nayana Motamma objects to elephant drive

Karnataka MLA questions scientific basis of elephant relocation

Chikkamagaluru MLAs demand action





BENGALURU: A dispute over the proposed relocation of wild elephants from Hassan to Chikkamagaluru escalated into a political confrontation on Monday, with Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitting her resignation letter to the Speaker's office.Objecting to the forest department's alleged decision to drive the animals into her Mudigere constituency without consulting local representatives, she said she would not continue in office if the lives and livelihoods of her constituents were put at risk.Motamma handed over the letter to the Speaker's personal secretary in the absence of Speaker G S Patil. She alleged that the forest department had started the elephant-driving operation without taking elected representatives from the affected areas into confidence, even though a meeting had already been scheduled to discuss the matter."I have to answer the people who elected me. I am not answerable merely to the government. If we cannot protect the people who elected us, what is the purpose of holding public office," she said at a press conference.The Mudigere legislator said she had brought her resignation letter to Vidhana Soudha after learning that forest officials had allegedly begun moving elephants towards her constituency without informing local MLAs or seeking their consent.According to Motamma, a herd of 56 elephants had recently passed through the Belur region of Hassan district, during which one or two people lost their lives. Another person was subsequently killed in the N R Pura region of Chikkamagaluru district.Following these incidents, Hassan district in-charge minister K M Shivalinge Gowda had reportedly suggested driving the elephants into the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary.Motamma said four MLAs from Chikkamagaluru district, including the Tarikere legislator, had submitted a written representation to the forest minister opposing the proposal.Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy had initially fixed November 25 for a meeting with legislators from Hassan and Chikkamagaluru districts. The meeting was later postponed to November 30, with a decision on the proposed relocation expected after discussions."How could the officials take a decision and begin the operation before that meeting? No elected representative from our side had agreed to the proposal," Motamma said.She said she was touring Kalasa on Sunday when she received information that elephants were being driven towards Mudigere from a location around three-and-a-half kilometres away.The operation was allegedly being supervised by Hassan forest officials and an Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (APCCF) associated with Project Elephant.At around 9 pm on Sunday, Motamma contacted the forest minister, the APCCF, Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) Pushkar and other senior officials to register her strong objection.Although the officials had assured her that the operation would not go ahead, she said she started receiving alerts from around 6 am on Monday that the elephants were being moved."I sent messages to the PCCF and the APCCF through SMS and WhatsApp, making my objection clear. It is highly condemnable that such an operation was undertaken without consulting or even informing the elected representatives of the affected areas," she said.Motamma said the chief minister and forest minister subsequently intervened after legislators raised objections. The Chief Conservators of Forests (CCFs) of Hassan and Chikkamagaluru also briefed them and assured the legislators that the operation would be halted and the status quo maintained.However, she insisted that elephants that had already been driven towards Mudigere must be sent back."If they are not taken back by tonight, I will resign tomorrow morning. I have come here with my resignation letter ready. I cannot accept a decision taken without consulting us," she said.Questioning the reasoning behind the proposed relocation, Motamma said officials had described the exercise as being based on scientific methods but had not explained the basis of their decision to elected representatives and other stakeholders."Neither the Planters' Association, nor the farmers' organisations, nor the local people or elected representatives were taken into confidence before arriving at this decision," she said.She also questioned whether the lives of people in Hassan were being given greater importance than those in Chikkamagaluru. Warning about the potential consequences of moving elephants into unfamiliar areas, she said the operation could endanger human lives, damage crops and affect livelihoods.Motamma said a herd of around 20 to 21 elephants had traditionally travelled through the region two or three times every year. Their usual route took them from Belur and Sakleshpur through Mudigere, Sringeri and Chikkamagaluru before they returned."There is no objection if the elephants move along their usual routes. But what the officials are now proposing is to forcibly drive them into our forests and leave them there. We cannot accept this under any circumstances," she said.She also asked who would be held accountable if the relocation resulted in crop destruction or further loss of human lives.Chikkamagaluru MLA T D Thammaiah, who shared the press conference platform with Motamma and Sringeri MLA T D Rajegowda, said human-animal conflict had increased considerably in the district over the past five to six years.He said four of the five MLAs from Chikkamagaluru had repeatedly raised the issue and written to the forest minister, PCCF and chief minister, opposing the movement of elephants from Hassan into their district.Thammaiah called for the immediate suspension of Hassan DFO Harish, alleging that the officer's actions had contributed to the deaths of two people in Hassan and the subsequent movement of elephants towards Mudigere.He said the elephants had traditionally remained around Tata Estate in Sakleshpur and Bikkod before undertaking their seasonal movement through Chikkamagaluru district.The legislators also urged the state government to ensure that the elephants were taken back to their original habitats. They warned against allowing the situation to escalate into a confrontation between local residents and forest officials.Motamma reiterated that she would go ahead with her resignation if the elephants were not sent back, maintaining that safeguarding the lives and livelihoods of her constituents mattered more to her than retaining her position as an MLA.'(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma objects to elephant drive in her constituency. She says forest officials had allegedly begun moving elephants towards her constituency without informing local MLAs or seeking their consent. A herd of 56 elephants had recently passed through the Belur region of Hassan district, during which one or two people lost their lives.

Article Title: Six schoolchildren injured as car hits e-rickshaw in Araria
Article Text:
Representational image

Patna:





Six schoolchildren were injured when a car collided head-on with an e-rickshaw carrying students in Araria district on Monday morning. The impact severed one child’s hand, which became trapped inside the car.The accident occurred around 7.30am near the Power House on the Araria-Raniganj road. The children were on their way to a private school in Kursipur when the car, coming from the opposite direction, hit their e-rickshaw. The car’s front was badly damaged. Locals rushed the injured to Araria Sadar Hospital.Doctors said six children were brought to the hospital, two of whom were in critical condition. They were referred to a higher medical centre in Purnia after initial treatment, while the other four are being treated and are out of danger.Dr Nirmal Kumar Mandal of Sadar Hospital said two children had sustained serious injuries and were referred to Purnia.“The injured receiving treatment at the hospital include Abu Hamwad (7), Zoya Parveen, Sania Firdaus and Mohammad Abidullah, besides e-rickshaw driver Mohammad Abid, 30,” he said.The driver sustained serious injuries to his head, face and near his eye and was unable to speak.School chairman Mohammad Shahjahan blamed the car driver for the accident and said only three to four children were injured, one of them relatively seriously.Traffic incharge SHO Khushbu Kumari said police reached the spot after receiving information and shifted the injured to hospital with the help of residents.“Both vehicles have been seized, and an investigation is underway. Police are examining the possibility of overloading and action would be taken if violations are established,” she said.District transport officer Sanjeev Kumar Sajjan said overloading was prohibited and e-rickshaws were not authorised to carry schoolchildren. He said an emergency meeting of the e-rickshaw drivers’ association had been called for Tuesday to explain the rules. The transport department would also write to the district education officer.District education officer Sahab Alam said the private school’s registration would be examined and action taken if irregularities were found. Police are investigating the collision and trying to identify the car driver.
Article Summary: Six schoolchildren were injured when a car collided head-on with an e-rickshaw carrying students in Araria district on Monday morning. The impact severed one child’s hand, which became trapped inside the car. The driver sustained serious injuries to his head, face and near his eye and was unable to speak.

Article Title: 10-year-old sexually assaulted in Delhi park by repeat offender months after release from jail; follows Aastha Kunj gang rape case
Article Text:
A 10-year-old girl was sexually assaulted in a park in northwest Delhi (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: A 10-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a man inside a park in northwest Delhi on November 24. The accused was caught and thrashed by local residents before being handed over to the police.The accused, identified as Rajesh, a resident of northwest Delhi, was previously convicted in a 2018 case involving the sexual assault of a minor in Swaroop Nagar and sentenced to seven years in prison. He was released from jail a few months ago, police sources said.According to police, a PCR call regarding the incident was received around 11.30 am, following which a team from the local police station rushed to the spot.The initial inquiry revealed that the girl, a Class IV student, was inside the park when the accused allegedly approached her and attempted to sexually assault her.There were also claims that she was passing through the park on her way to a relative's house after school, which police have denied.Hearing the girl's screams, people in the vicinity rushed to help her, caught the accused and assaulted him before handing him over to the police.Police sources said the 35-year-old accused was unmarried and had allegedly been estranged from his family. Investigators are also probing whether he was under the influence of any intoxicating substance at the time of the incident. His blood samples have been sent for testing.His electronic devices are being seized and examined as part of the investigation, including to check his internet search history. Police will also investigate whether he was involved in similar incidents after his release from jail that may have gone unreported.The incident has also raised questions over security arrangements at the park. Police sources said the sprawling park had only one guard deployed at the time of the incident, despite requiring at least four to five personnel for effective monitoring."The park is quite large and requires at least four to five guards, but only one was present when the incident took place. We had earlier flagged the security concern with the concerned authorities and will pursue the matter further," a police source said.The incident comes two months after three men posing as policemen allegedly threatened and gang-raped a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi's Kalkaji.The girl told police that she visited Kalkaji Temple with her friend on her birthday, September 22, and later entered Aastha Kunj Park. The two were sitting near the swings when three men, aged between 30 and 35, allegedly approached them, slapped her friend and posed as policemen.When she resisted, one of the men allegedly threatened her by showing a gun. The trio then took out knives, led her to a secluded part of the park and allegedly sexually assaulted her.
Article Summary: A 10-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a man inside a park in northwest Delhi on November 24. The accused was caught and thrashed by local residents before being handed over to the police. Police sources said the sprawling park had only one guard deployed at the time of the incident.

Article Title: Accredited vs self-proclaimed: SC to examine protection for journalists
Article Text:
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that journalistic freedom has to be balanced with the administration of public order and law.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday referred allegations of police assault, manhandling and wrongful detention of seven journalists covering protests in Delhi in October to a high-powered inquiry committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice R Subhash Reddy.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit relevant material before the five-member committee, which will examine the allegations and establish whether the journalists were subjected to police excesses.The petitions were filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) and the Delhi Union of Journalists over alleged police action against media personnel covering protests on October 10 and 11, 2026. The demonstrations were reportedly demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Justice Bagchi said the committee would ascertain whether the journalists were present at the protest sites, whether force was used against them and, if so, whether it was excessive in the circumstances."You will go back to the committee which we have constituted to factually demonstrate whether your petitioners were, in fact, present there.If present, whether they were subjected to excessive force," he observed, as quoted by PTI.The judge added that the committee should examine whether the force used was disproportionate to what was necessary for maintaining public order.The bench also indicated that it would consider broader constitutional questions concerning the protection available to journalists covering protests and public events, including whether accredited journalists are entitled to greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters.Justice Bagchi observed that self-proclaimed journalists may not enjoy the same protection as accredited media persons.Appearing for the journalists, senior advocate PV Dinesh said the seven media personnel worked for established news organisations and were not social media reel-makers."We are just journalists, recognised journalists. Allow us to do our work," he submitted.He also questioned whether journalists working for established media organisations could be taken into custody while performing their professional duties."The question is, when established journalists, who are recognised journalists, are covering events, can they be taken into custody?" Dinesh asked, as quoted by PTI.The court indicated that it would examine the constitutional safeguards available to journalists, including their freedom of movement and right to practise their profession. It would also consider whether forcibly removing a journalist from a location amounts to custody and the legal consequences of such action.The petitioners alleged that journalists were forcibly removed from reporting locations, prevented from recording events and subjected to physical force despite displaying their press credentials. The allegations also include an attempt to snatch a photographer's camera and the physical assault of a woman journalist while she was reporting live.The seven journalists named in the petition are Suhail Muhammed and VS Rahul of 24 News, Sajin of Asianet News, Roshni Rajan and Farsana of Reporter TV, Vishnuprasad of Mathrubhumi and Miji P Jose of Manorama News.The Delhi Police had earlier told the Supreme Court that social media influencers and reel-makers cannot claim the same protections as journalists covering protests.In an affidavit, the police described journalists as a "distinct category" from social media content creators who use cameras and microphones to make reels for commercial gain. It argued that the latter cannot automatically claim the protections available to the press while reporting from protest sites.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court referred allegations of police assault, manhandling and wrongful detention of seven journalists to a high-powered inquiry committee. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit relevant material before the committee. The petitions were filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) and the Delhi Union of Journalists.

Article Title: 'Wanted to take over Rs 6 crore business': How UP woman slow-poisoned husband, son, nephew for a year
Article Text:
Renu, who was arrested on Nov 23, has allegedly revealed during interrogation that she wanted full control of her husband’s transport business.

FIR Names Mom, Bro

6cr biz, 2cr insurance: Money, control motives in poisoning plot





GHAZIABAD: A 42-year-old woman was arrested for allegedly trying to slow-poison her husband, son and nephew at their house in Vasundhara by spiking their food with small doses of lead regularly over a period of at least 12 months.Renu, who was arrested on Nov 23, has allegedly revealed during interrogation she wanted full control of her husband's transport business, which currently has an annual turnover of around Rs 6 crore.Police said Renu was taken into custody from her sister's house in Delhi's Jhilmil Colony after a preliminary investigation following an FIR in Sept based on a complaint by Sushil Kumar Bhatnagar (45), her husband. In his complaint, Bhatnagar claimed he had fallen severely ill on Aug 21 last year, and tests done at a private facility showed high levels of lead in his blood samples. He remained admitted at Max Hospital in Vaishali for two months.Bhatnagar told police he fell ill again later that year and was admitted to hospital for a second time. Doctors diagnosed him with chronic lead poisoning. He said his 16-year-old son Vansh and 21-year-old nephew Dev Bhatnagar also took ill over the next few months and recovery took weeks. DCP trans-Hindon Rijul said Bhatnagar began to suspect Renu when medical reports of all three victims showed lead poisoning.DCP trans-Hindon Rijul told TOI Bhatnagar began to suspect Renu when medical reports of all three victims showed lead poisoning. "Bhatnagar, however, did not have any evidence at the time. He told police that in the first week of Sept this year, his 12-year-old daughter told him Renu would set aside portions for the mother-daughter before 'spraying something on the food' she served to the rest of the family," the DCP said.When Bhatnagar confronted Renu, she allegedly didn't respond and instead went to his sister's house in Delhi. On Sept 24, Bhatnagar submitted a complaint at Indirapuram police station. An FIR was registered against Renu under BNS sections 109 (attempt to murder), 123 (causing hurt by poison or drugs) and 61 (2) (criminal conspiracy). Four others, including her mother Lata Saxena, her brother Ravi, her brother-in-law Sushil Girdhar and an acquaintance Bablu, were also named in the FIR for conniving."Police recorded the statement of the girl, doctors and reviewed the reports of the three victims. After initial investigation, police found substantial evidence that Renu was administering poison to her husband, son and nephew between 2024 and 2025," the DCP said.After her arrest, Renu is said to have told police she mixed lead in small quantities in the food she served to her husband, son and nephew. "Renu claimed she wanted to take over his travel agency. So, she decided to kill Bhatnagar and nephew Dev, who is the caretaker of the business. Renu also tried to kill her son as he backed his father," Rijul said. Renu was also the nominee for Bhatnagar's life insurance policy worth Rs 2 crore.The DCP said police are trying to determine where the woman bought the poison or if someone gave it to her. Police are also investigating whether others were involved. She threw the poison into a trash bin somewhere before leaving her husband's house in Sept, a police officer said.According to doctors, chronic lead poisoning often causes no obvious early symptoms even as lead builds up in the body and harms organs. When symptoms appear over weeks, months or years, they vary by age and commonly affect the digestive, nervous, cardiovascular and reproductive systems. "Lead poisoning can cause death if exposure is severe or treatment is delayed. Extremely high levels of lead can cause seizures, coma and permanent brain damage," said Dr Sanjay Teotia, former CMS of Sanjay Nagar Hospital in Ghaziabad.The case has similarities with Keralam's Koodathayi cyanide murder case, where a woman, Jolly Joseph, was accused of killing six members of her family between 2002 and 2016.The victims included her mother-in-law Annamma Thomas, father-in-law Tom Thomas, first husband Roy Thomas, Annamma's brother Mathew Manjadiyil, and Sily and her two-year-old daughter Alphine. Investigators alleged that Joseph used cyanide, mixed with food or drinks, to poison five victims. She allegedly used veterinary poison, sold as 'dog kill', to murder Annamma. Police suspected property disputes and her desire to marry Sily's husband as motives. Arrested in Oct 2019, Joseph faces six murder cases. Today, she remains in jail as an undertrial; the case is still being heard.
Article Summary: 42-year-old woman arrested for allegedly trying to slow-poison her husband, son and nephew. She allegedly spiking their food with small doses of lead regularly over a period of at least 12 months. Renu, who was arrested on Nov 23, has allegedly revealed during interrogation that she wanted full control of her husband’s transport business.

Article Title: 85-year-old man sought to evict his son and daughter-in-law from self-acquired Delhi home, but authorities rejected plea over lack of proof of harassment; Delhi High Court overturns their orders and g
Article Text:
Ultimately, the High Court held that an elderly parent should not be compelled to share his home against his wishes. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why Delhi High Court asked son & daughter to vacate

Ravi Kant Gupta v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.

Pritam Singh v. Government of NCT of Delhi & Ors.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Can children forcefully continue to live in their parents’ self-acquired property if the latter ask them to vacate? An 85-year-old man has secured relief with the Delhi High Court asking his son and daughter-in-law to vacate the property.The court held that a senior citizen seeking eviction under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, does not necessarily have to prove that his children have ill-treated him.An elderly man owns a flat which he acquired from the Delhi Development Authority in 1980 and converted it into freehold in 2000. His eldest son and daughter-in-law had been living there since their marriage in 2003.The man claimed that he had asked the couple to arrange alternative accommodation after his second son married in 2005 and his youngest son married in 2008. He alleged that the couple refused to leave, that their behaviour towards him deteriorated over the years and that they stopped supporting him financially. He further claimed that their harassment intensified after his wife died in November 2020.The father alleged that in 2022, the couple threatened him and assaulted his youngest son.He said he filed a police complaint and subsequently approached the authorities under the 2007 Act, seeking eviction and maintenance.The District Magistrate rejected his application in 2023, observing that the allegations had not been proved and that the Act was being used to resolve a business dispute between the sons.The father appealed and in June 2025, the Divisional Commissioner set aside the original order and sent the matter back for reconsideration because the first inquiry had not determined whether the complaint was genuine.A fresh enquiry report again concluded that harassment had not been established. The District Magistrate rejected the application and the Divisional Commissioner upheld that decision in April 2026.The father then approached the Delhi High Court. His counsel argued that, as the property's absolute owner, he was entitled to live there peacefully and that proof of ill-treatment was not a prerequisite for eviction.The respondents disputed his account. Their counsel argued that the complaint had been made at the instance of the father's younger son amid a business dispute between the brothers. They also maintained that they had been looking after the father and had offered to pay him Rs 15,000 a month as maintenance.The Delhi High Court noted that the father's ownership was undisputed. The son and daughter-in-law had not claimed ownership rights over the property and were living there because of their relationship with him. The father had also made it clear that he no longer wished to share his home with them.The court relied on the Supreme Court's August 4, 2026, decision in, which recognised that tribunals under the Senior Citizens Act could order eviction where necessary to protect a senior citizen.It also referred to the Delhi High Court's earlier ruling in, which recognised that proof of ill-treatment was not invariably necessary if the property needed protection so the senior citizen could live peacefully.The court found that the authorities had made proof of harassment an essential condition without considering whether the property needed protection.It criticised the first enquiry report for being inconclusive, observing: “A report which is, on its own showing, inconclusive could not have formed the basis of a finding that the allegations of harassment stood disproved.”The authorities had also failed to adequately consider the father's repeated police complaints and an earlier High Court direction requiring the police to assist him against any threat from the respondents.The existence of a business dispute between the brothers, the court said, could not by itself justify rejecting the father's grievance.As the judgment put it: “Merely because there may also exist a business dispute between the sons of the petitioner, the same, by itself, cannot be a ground to hold that the grievance of the petitioner is not genuine, or to deny him the protection afforded under the Act.”Ultimately, the High Court held that an elderly parent should not be compelled to share his home against his wishes when the relationship has deteriorated to the point of prolonged litigation.The Delhi High Court observed: “At the age of 85 years, the petitioner is entitled to live in his own house peacefully and with dignity.”The court set aside the Divisional Commissioner's order and the District Magistrate's order. It directed the son and daughter-in-law to vacate the property within four weeks and instructed the concerned Station House Officer to provide the necessary assistance if required.Adnan Siddiqui, Partner at King Stubb & Kasiva, told ET that father prevailed before the Delhi High Court because he is the absolute owner of the DDA flat.Neither his son nor his daughter-in-law has any independent interest in the property, as they were permitted to live there only with his consent. After the father decided that they could no longer stay in the flat because of the harassment he had faced, the Delhi High Court upheld his decision.Siddiqui says: "This case is significant as it highlights that, in addition to aspects relating to property, the entitlement of older people to live in their own home is also associated with their safety, and both mental and physical wellbeing."
Article Summary: The court held that a senior citizen seeking eviction under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, does not necessarily have to prove that his children have ill-treated him. Ultimately, the High Court held that an elderly parent should not be compelled to share his home against his wishes.

Tamil Nadu has approved 15 days of paternity leave for male government employees

Article Title: Panna tigress dies after getting entangled in clutch-wire trap laid for wild boars; carcass found in North Forest Division, teams launch probe as MP tiger toll rises to 60
Article Text:
A tigress was found dead, trapped in a clutch-wire snare reportedly laid by poachers

Key highlights

Panna tiger





1. A tigress died after getting entangled in a clutch-wire trap allegedly laid by poachers in Panna's North Forest Division.2. The carcass was found in the Manki-Katariya forest on Wednesday, prompting a joint investigation by forest teams.3. Preliminary findings suggest the trap had been laid to catch wild boars.4. The death takes Madhya Pradesh's reported tiger mortality toll this year to at least 60.5. Forest officials are trying to identify those responsible for laying the trap and establish the circumstances leading to the tigress's death.BHOPAL: A tigress died after getting caught in a deadly clutch-wire trap allegedly laid by poachers in the Manki-Katariya forest under Panna's North Forest Division, taking Madhya Pradesh's reported tiger mortality toll to at least 60 this year.The carcass was found on Wednesday. Teams from Panna Tiger Reserve and the North Forest Division rushed to the spot and launched an investigation.Preliminary findings suggest that the clutch-wire trap had been laid to catch wild boars. The tigress got entangled in it and died. Forest officials are trying to identify those who laid the trap and establish the circumstances leading to her death.The state's reported tiger death toll stood at 59 on November 19, following the death of a male tiger in Bandhavgarh's Manpur buffer zone.The death of the tigress in Panna takes the toll to at least 60.A clutch-wire trap is designed to tighten its grip as the trapped animal struggles to escape. Each movement pulls the wire tighter around its body or limb, increasing pressure and restricting blood flow.The tightening wire can cause deep wounds, severe tissue damage and blood loss, eventually killing the animal if it remains trapped, officials said.Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey has demanded strong action in the matter, calling it a case of grave negligence on the part of forest officials. He also said that the North Panna division has now turned into a death trap for tigers.
Article Summary: A tigress was found dead, trapped in a clutch-wire snare reportedly laid by poachers. The carcass was found in the Manki-Katariya forest under Panna's North Forest Division. The death takes Madhya Pradesh's reported tiger mortality toll this year to at least 60.

Article Title: In Manipur, a glass of drinking water comes at a price: Women trek through forests, villagers risk ambushes to repair pipelines amid conflict and drought
Article Text:
A woman collects water from a roadside source in Manipur. Photo: Ismat Ara

Daily burden: A woman carries a basin of water on her head as residents navigate the daily struggle to secure water in conflict-hit Manipur. Photo: Ismat Ara





IMPHAL: In parts of Manipur, getting drinking water means walking through forests in search of a spring. Repairing a broken pipeline can be even more dangerous. In May, villagers from Konsakhul in Kangpokpi were ambushed while attempting to restore a damaged community pipeline. Two months earlier, two youths had died after setting out to repair water pipelines near the Ukhrul-Kamjong border, over 100km away.With Manipur recording a 45% deficit in monsoon rainfall, according to IMD, the onset of winter has brought fresh anxieties for communities already grappling with damaged infrastructure, shrinking natural sources and restrictions on movement.In hilly districts, where direct tap water often remains largely absent outside some district headquarters, villages have traditionally depended on natural springs and rainwater harvesting, according to wetlands and Loktak Lake activist Ram Wangkheirakpam. But several springs are now drying up, leaving communities with fewer reliable sources. “The conflict has made it harder to reach water sources and maintain supply lines,” Wangkheirakpam told TOI.The burden often falls on women, who walk long distances through forested stretches to fetch water. What was once a familiar part of village life has become more difficult as natural sources recede and movement across conflict-divided areas remains fraught.“In districts like Senapati, Ukhrul, and Chandel, villages marked 'covered' on paper, women and children still walk kilometre-long distances daily to fetch water from streams, springs, or community wells,” Wangkheirakpam told TOI, adding that in Imphal, too, municipal taps offer little assurance. “Households receive piped water for barely one to two hours, twice a week... Many have turned to private tankers, paying Rs 300-500 for 500-1,000 litres. ”And for the 60,000-plus people displaced by the conflict and living across relief camps, the struggle is more immediate. At Churachandpur’s Tuibung Community Hall, 150 residents from 23 families share three toilets and pool their ?84 daily relief allowance to buy drinking water. At nearby Mandap camp, where 250 people remain in makeshift shelters, only two of eight toilets work—leaving residents like Hatnu, in her twenties, with little privacy to bathe or manage periods alongside a daily struggle for clean water.In Senapati, social activist R K Paul Chawang told TOI villagers “wake up as early as 3.30-4am in the winter cold to collect water from common points”, taking turns with buckets. Along with five Naga communities in 2025, Chawang filed a PIL in Manipur HC over alleged irregularities in Jal Jeevan Mission projects.Contacted for comment, a senior official in the Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), which executes drinking-water projects, said rural coverage was split into two streams: 38% under the Centre's Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)—still awaiting Gram Sabha certification—and 62% under a New Development Bank-funded project. Work on the latter was progressing, the official said, adding that “discrepancies in online records were being corrected” and “village water supply had improved. ”
Article Summary: In parts of Manipur, getting drinking water means walking through forests in search of a spring. In May, villagers from Konsakhul in Kangpokpi were ambushed while attempting to restore a damaged community pipeline. Two months earlier, two youths had died after setting out to repair water pipelines near the Ukhrul- Kamjong border.

Article Title: In 2015, MP man buys TV for Rs 31,500 with 3-year warranty, alleges it stopped displaying pictures in 2018; claims company ignored toll-free complaint, state consumer commission rejects appeal over la
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





BHOPAL: A Tikamgarh man’s complaint against a television that allegedly stopped displaying pictures has been rejected by Madhya Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. The commission held that he failed to establish that the set had developed a manufacturing defect during the warranty period or that he had formally complained to the seller.The commission dismissed the appeal on Nov 20, upholding Tikamgarh District Consumer Commission’s order rejecting his complaint. Manoj Kumar Dixit had purchased a television for Rs 31,500 from an electronics retailer on Nov 10, 2015. He claimed that the set came with a three-year warranty but developed a problem with its picture display during the warranty period. He sought repair or replacement of the television.Dixit said he subsequently sent a notice to the seller and also raised a complaint through the company’s toll-free number on Oct 25, 2018. However, he alleged that no action was taken. The retailer denied responsibility, arguing that it was only the retailer and not the manufacturer. It said Dixit had never complained to it about the television being defective. The manufacturer and its other respondent entity did not appear before the district commission, which proceeded ex parte against them.Challenging the dismissal of his complaint, Dixit argued before the state commission that the district commission had failed to properly examine the documents and submissions on record.However, the state commission found that he had not specified the date on which the television developed the alleged fault. He had also failed to produce an expert report establishing a manufacturing defect or documents showing that he had complained to the respondents about the problem. The commission observed that, in the absence of such evidence, it could not be established that the television had developed a manufacturing defect during the warranty period. It found no deficiency in service on the part of the respondents and dismissed the appeal as meritless.The order was passed by a bench headed by commission president Justice Sunita Yadav, with Dr Monika Malik as member.
Article Summary: Manoj Kumar Dixit had purchased a television for Rs 31,500 from an electronics retailer. He claimed that the set came with a three-year warranty but developed a problem with its picture display during the warranty period. He sought repair or replacement of the television.
